product.ta-1100c.summary: The TA 1100 C built two floppy drives into a more compact workstation than the TA 1100.
product.ta-1100c.history: Triumph-Adler offered it to small and medium-sized businesses. Computerwoche reported a DM 36,000 offer in 1979. The UPV museum dates its commercial introduction to 1981.
product.ta-1100c.technical.configuration: The screen displayed office work. The factory brochure specifies 48 columns by 22 rows. The UPV museum reports 44 by 24.
product.ta-1100c.technical.verified: BluMach has no runnable profile for this model.
product.ta-1100c.technical.limitations: The 24 KB of MOS PROM documented in the brochure and a system disk remain to be recovered.
